definitions.meaning: read literally, a sitter arriving to mind the children calls in order to mind them

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the duties of baby-sitters who come round to look after children.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as CALL (visit) TO MIND (look after children).
explanation.definitionFit: To call something to mind is an idiom for recalling it from memory.

indicators.note: the river runs across the alley, so its letter sits within the passage

parts.note: a cut is a narrow passage or short cut, an alley

explanation.surface: A brief alley that crosses a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt describes a reply that is brief to the point of rudeness.

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A council member who is fairly nimble.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome means supple and lithe, moving with easy grace.

clue.text: Sneak giving indication that it is an obvious clue

parts.note: a sneak or telltale tells tales on others
a sign is an indication

explanation.surface: A sneak giving away that something is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clue' here means evidence, not a crossword clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign is a revealing piece of evidence that gives something away.

definitions.meaning: stuff, the matter or fabric something is made of
... evidence is relevant and significant to the matter

explanation.definitionFit: Cloth or substance is material, and a fact bearing on a case is material to it.

clue.text: Knight with endless abundance, but only one bit of pasta

parts.note: N is the chess abbreviation for knight

indicators.note: the word for abundance loses its final letter

parts.note: oodles means an abundance, lots

explanation.surface: A knight with plenty of food, yet just one strand of pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only one' explains the singular: oodles of noodles less the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is a single strip of pasta, the singular of a common dish.

definitions.meaning: read as 'nipper is': a creature with pincers that nips, here the seashore crustacean
a small sour wild apple shares the crustacean's name; the question mark flags the shortened form

explanation.surface: Asking which apple belongs to a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nipper' looks like British slang for a small child; here it is a pincered creature, and the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pinching shellfish and the sour wild fruit tree share one name.

clue.text: Raise a collection of suspects perhaps

definitions.meaning: to ... a figure is to raise it to the next whole number
a gathering of people, such as police collecting suspects

explanation.definitionFit: Numbers are rounded up to a higher value, and police make a round-up of likely culprits.

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: battled means fought
4 down is MATERIAL, and raw material extracted from the ground is ore

explanation.surface: A noisy dispute fought over raw stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: A battledore is the small racket used in the old game of battledore and shuttlecock. 'Racket' looks like noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The battledore was a light bat used to hit a shuttlecock, an early form of badminton racket.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a solution is the answer to a problem

explanation.surface: Engineers delivering their verdict on a technical answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A resolution is a formal decision or ruling reached by a body, much like a judgement.

indicators.note: the word for train has its final letter cut off, losing its end

parts.note: a suite is a train of attendants or retinue

explanation.surface: A dress or outfit with a long train that seems to go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like part of a wedding dress, but it means a retinue (SUITE).
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is a set of matching clothes worn together, an outfit.

clue.text: Played part of individual I married going round

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces encircles the word for individual

parts.note: mated means paired off or married
a person is an individual

explanation.surface: An actor who married someone playing a role.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who impersonated a figure portrayed or acted as them on stage.

definitions.meaning: a flash of lightning, as in a thunderbolt

explanation.definitionFit: A streak of lightning is a bolt, and fleeing in haste is bolting away.

clue.text: Older male upset, getting nothing for a perfect example

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over and thrown into a new order
nothing taking the place of a means one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: An older man is distressed at receiving nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting nothing for a' swaps the A in OLDER MALE for O; 'upset' then rearranges OLDERMOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person whose conduct others copy, an ideal pattern to follow.

indicators.note: the regular letters come after the word for prayer

parts.note: a collect is a short prayer in Christian liturgy

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone who disowns the church offering after prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of disowns give ION.
explanation.definitionFit: The offertory is the church collection of money taken during a service.

clue.text: Please turn to next page to see it

definitions.text: Please turn to next page to see it

parts.words: Please turn to next page to see it
parts.note: the instruction that a reader will find something by turning the page describes text located on the other side of the sheet

explanation.surface: A printed instruction telling a reader to turn the page.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like the PTO note at the foot of a page; the answer is where 'it' is found.
explanation.definitionFit: Overleaf means on the reverse side of the sheet, reached by turning the page.

parts.note: key means essential, as in a key factor
a pad is a flat, an apartment

explanation.surface: An essential flat component of a pocket calculator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an adjective describing the part; it is the noun PAD, a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A keypad is the panel of buttons on a calculator; the question mark marks this as one example.

clue.text: Side having necessary willingness for cricket, say

parts.note: a side is a team
to be game is to be willing to have a go

explanation.surface: A cricket side with the right attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket is one example of a sport played by teams; 'say' flags the example.

clue.text: Exact place and time for destructive insect

parts.note: a locus is a particular position or exact place

explanation.surface: Pinpointing where and when a crop-eating insect will strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts swarm and strip crops bare, the classic ravaging pest.

parts.note: chic means stylish
ken is range of knowledge, as in beyond one's ken

explanation.surface: Meat cooked on a stylish kitchen range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a cooker; it is KEN, scope of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is poultry flesh eaten as food.

parts.note: fellows are men
to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: Men swearing at their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Menswear is the garments sold for males, a category of apparel.

clue.text: Former lover seen with Pope from a prosperous area

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
Urban is the name taken by eight popes

explanation.surface: A former lover spotted with the Pope, from a rich district.
explanation.definitionFit: Exurban describes the well-off region beyond the suburbs where commuters live.

clue.text: Remove dodgy nightclub's permit, at last

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable nightclub; with the 's it gives dives

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of permit

explanation.surface: Taking away a seedy club's licence at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to strip or deprive someone of something.

clue.text: Cold fish with glaze — it keeps food fresh

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family
a glaze is a thin film or coating

explanation.surface: A cold fish dish glazed and wrapped to stay fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Cling film is thin plastic wrap stretched over dishes to preserve leftovers.

clue.text: Talent ineffectual for the most part

indicators.note: only most of the phrase is kept, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: something ineffectual is no use

explanation.surface: Talent that is mostly useless.
explanation.walkthrough: NO USE loses its last letter; NOUS is British informal for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is practical intelligence or know-how, a gift for getting things done.

indicators.note: the chopper sits outside, wrapping around the letter for left

parts.note: an axe is a chopper

explanation.surface: A rod left beside a chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the bar on which wheels turn.

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the first and last letters of the place name are taken

explanation.surface: Something dark on the fringes of a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Keighley is a town in West Yorkshire; its outskirts are K and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky means as dark as ink, deep black.

clue.text: Case following punishment that's found on pitch

indicators.note: the word for case comes after the word for punishment in the answer

parts.note: a penalty is a punishment
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A court case following a punishment, with a hint of the football field.
explanation.walkthrough: The penalty box is the marked area in front of each goal on a football pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The penalty area is a rectangle marked out on a soccer field, so it is literally on the pitch.

clue.text: Square meal ultimately ignored by returning Russian leader

indicators.note: returning sends the remaining letters back the other way
a letter ignored by the leader is left out of his name

parts.note: Lenin led the Bolshevik revolution in Russia

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of meal

explanation.surface: A Russian leader turning down a square meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square meal' looks like one phrase; 'Square' alone is the definition. LENIN without L gives ENIN, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a square number, three times three.

parts.note: everyone who turns up counts towards the tally of people at an event

explanation.surface: A riddle about who is included among those present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those present' is itself a common sense of the answer; the clue says they make it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The attendance is the number of people present at an event, so those there are counted in it.
